plan: Trim SPY to 20% to cure concentration and meet the mandate.
Sell all SOXL and SPAL to zero, eliminating leveraged ETF exposure.
Add to QQQI, increasing income exposure and favoring quality names.
Buy GLD for diversification and to add a top-quality name.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and diversifying holdings. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to cure concentration and meet the mandate.
Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2%, reducing leveraged ETF exposure.
Buy MSTR at 4% to add a strong scanner setup.
Add to QQQI to balance income and growth.
This plan aims for risk-first growth with a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month, aiming for risk-first growth. It reduces overall concentration and maintains a small allocation to leveraged ETFs. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a blend of broad market and quality tech exposure.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to cure concentration and meet the mandate.
Add to SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6%, increasing leveraged ETF exposure.
Buy MSTR at 6%, concentrating in a highest-scoring scanner setup.
Buy SQQQ at 3% to hedge against tech concentration.
This plan aims for stretch growth with a smaller cash buffer and strict stops.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. This mode carries substantially higher risk, including larger potential drawdowns and daily decay from leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Trim SPY to 20% to cure concentration and meet the mandate.
Sell all SOXL and SPAL to zero, eliminating leveraged ETF exposure.
Add to QQQI, prioritizing income and monthly distributions.
Buy GLD for diversification and to add a quality name.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, prioritizing steady monthly distributions and low drawdown. It eliminates leveraged ETFs and high-beta names, focusing on income and broad index exposure. While aiming for reliable income, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
